title: ADR: structured-embeddings-and-streaming-contract-2026
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:

This ADR records a cross-domain decision to standardize a lightweight contract for combined streaming generation and embeddings requests. The goal is to enable safe, predictable evolution of the API surface used by: the edge-proxy, model-router, embed-service, stream-gateway, and telemetry-pipeline.

Decision:

We adopt a dual-track contract: a strict structured payload (JSON Schema v1) for non-streaming embeddings and metadata, and a chained streaming envelope for long-running generation that can optionally carry incremental embedding updates. Both tracks share a compact version header and a capability bitset so routers and sidecars can negotiate fallback behavior.

Motivation and context:

- Customers increasingly send mixed workloads (short embeddings, long-chat streaming) through a single integration.
- We observed inconsistent handling of incremental embeddings in streaming sessions (loss of context, inconsistent attribution to requests), leading to troubleshooting overhead and customer-facing AE cases.
- Current ad-hoc approaches create high coupling between model variants and clients, making model version rollouts risky.

Constraints and non-goals:

- Non-goal: This ADR does not redesign the SDK; it constrains server-side contracts that SDKs will implement.
- Constraint: Must be implementable without rewriting the existing stream-gateway; changes should be additive with config flags.
- Constraint: Must preserve per-tenant billing attribution and SLO observability (no silent sampling of embeddings).

Alternatives considered:

1) Do nothing: continue with ad-hoc incrementals. Rejected — causes operational burden and regressions during rollouts.

2) Separate endpoints: force embeddings and streaming to different endpoints. Rejected — breaks customer ergonomics and increases egress/ingress complexity for private deployments.

3) Heavyweight protobuf/RPC contract with binary frames and full schema registry. Rejected — too heavyweight for quick iteration and cross-region private deployments that prefer JSON.

Chosen approach (details):

- Contract header: Every request MUST include a top-level header object "ri_contract" with fields: version (semver string), capability_mask (integer bitmask), request_id (UUID), tenant_id (string).

- Two tracks: 
  - Structured track (embeddings): a single JSON payload with schema 'embedding_request' (see example). This is the canonical path for batch or single embeddings.
  - Streaming track (generation + optional incr-embeds): an envelope with newline-delimited JSON frames. Each frame MUST include a frame_type field ("init", "token", "embed_delta", "final"). embed_delta frames carry embedding vectors for the partial text prefix with provenance metadata.

Examples:

Structured embedding request (HTTP POST):

POST /v2/structure/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "ri_contract": {"version": "1.0.0", "capability_mask": 0, "request_id": "b4d3-...", "tenant_id": "acme-corp"},
  "input": ["How to tune batching for latency?", "Redwood inference architecture"],
  "model": "redwood-emb-1.2",
  "response_options": {"normalize": true, "vector_format": "float16"}
}

Streaming envelope (HTTP chunked or WebSocket NDJSON):

{"ri_contract": {"version":"1.0.0","capability_mask":2,"request_id":"req-123","tenant_id":"acme-corp"}, "frame_type":"init","params":{"model":"redwood-gen-7b"}}
{"frame_type":"token","token":"Hello"}
{"frame_type":"token","token":" world"}
{"frame_type":"embed_delta","cursor":11,"embedding": [0.12, -0.03, ...], "provenance": {"prefix":"Hello world","prefix_len":11}}
{"frame_type":"final","completion_metadata":{"tokens":12}}

Capability mask bitset (initial):

- 0x01: supports_structured_embeddings
- 0x02: supports_streaming_embeds
- 0x04: accepts_incremental_routing_hints

Compatibility matrix (text table):

| Component | v1.0.0 header | streaming frames | embedDelta support | notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| edge-proxy | yes | passthrough | no | will add validation at parse step |
| stream-gateway | yes | must parse | yes | will buffer and validate embedding vectors |
| model-router | yes | understands frame_types | yes | may drop embed_delta when model variant cannot produce vects |
| telemetry-pipeline | yes | will accept event stream | yes | tag-based attribution required |
Implications:

API standards:
- Add ri_contract header to API spec and SDK generator templates.
- Register new endpoints (/v2/structure/embeddings and /v2/streaming/ndjson) in the public API catalog with stable docs.

Coding standards & infra:
- Server-side JSON parsing must be tolerant: accept unknown fields but fail-fast on missing ri_contract.
- Add a lightweight request validator library (go/python) packaged as an internal pip/go module. This module will implement schema checks and capability_mask helpers.
- Stream-gateway will implement adaptive backpressure: if embed_delta frames exceed 1MB/s per-request, gateway returns 429 with a structured retry-after JSON.

Model-serving and runtime behavior:
- Model variants that cannot produce embedding deltas must advertise capability_mask bit 0x02 == 0; model-router will fall back to post-hoc embeddings via embed-service and mark the request with a routing_reason header.
- For private deployments the runtime-sidecar will expose a toggle (ENV REDWOOD_ACCEPT_EMBED_DELTAS) defaulting to true for compatibility, but constrained by CPU caps.

Observability standards:
- New metrics: ri.requests_total, ri.stream.frames_by_type{frame_type}, ri.embed_vectors_bytes, ri.embed_generation_latency_ms (percentiles P50/P95).
- Tracing: Every frame must propagate the request_id and a frame_sequence integer. Spans must be created per-stream with child spans for embed-generation and model-inference.
- Alerts: if ri.embed_vectors_bytes per-tenant > 10GB/day unexpected, trigger investigate-embed-surge playbook.

Performance standards and SLOs:
- Streaming request p95 end-to-end latency (first token) must remain under 150ms for hosted-critical tier.
- Embedding generation SLO: 99th percentile per-item embedding time < 80ms for small models and < 250ms for large batch variants.
- The stream-gateway should enforce a soft limit of 100 embed_delta frames per minute per request by default.

Migration and rollout plan (phased):

1) Stage 0 (feature-gated dev): ship request validator library and unit tests; default flags off in prod.
2) Stage 1 (internal rollout): enable header validation in internal staging, update stream-gateway to parse frame_type but continue passthrough behavior. Add telemetry dashboards.
3) Stage 2 (public opt-in): publish API docs; SDKs add header template; allow customers to opt into streaming embed deltas via account flag.
4) Stage 3 (enforce): require ri_contract for all v2 endpoints; stream-gateway returns 400 on missing header.

Testing and validation:
- QA harness: replay 10M historical requests through a staging stream-gateway to validate parsing and observe embed vector distribution.
- Perf test matrix: small (redwood-emb-1), medium (redwood-emb-1.2), large (redwood-gen-7b) across GPU types (A100, L40s) with synthetic loads.
- Backwards-compat tests: simulate model-router fallback and validate billing attribution remains correct.

Operational runbooks and playbooks:
- Investigate-embed-surge: steps to identify tenant, disable embed_delta via tenant feature toggle, revert model-variant if sudden surge coincides with recent rollout.
- Fallback-to-post-hoc: how to rehydrate missing embed_delta frames by re-sending final text to embed-service and adding mapping metadata.

Open questions and future work:
- Schema: whether to move from JSON Schema to a compact CBOR wire format after initial stabilization for bandwidth savings.
- Delta compression: research efficient lossy compression for embed_delta frames to reduce network cost for high-frequency partials.

Owners and contacts:
- RFC author / primary owner: Aisha Patel (serving-runtime)
